reason: The text passage (Exodus 16) discusses God testing the Israelites' willingness to follow His commandments and laws regarding the gathering of manna and observance of the Sabbath. While it shows God's disapproval of those who refuse to keep His commandments ('How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?'), it contains no explicit threat or statement that Yahweh will kill the Hebrews as a consequence. The text describes implicit consequences—such as finding no manna on the seventh day—but does not mention killing, death, or lethal punishment as a result of improper worship or failure to follow the laws.
